A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete 46-page contents, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original PDE experiments, sparse-observation inference, and natural-image fine-tuning results in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including numerical residual and distributional metrics, ablations, and generated samples in Section 4 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The joint state–parameter evolution, inverse predictor, weak-residual objective, scaled noise schedule, regularization, and training/sampling algorithms are unchanged. The equation-notation corrections do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover Darcy flow, linear elasticity, Helmholtz, Stokes flow, sparse-observation guidance, and natural-image recoloring. Noise, boundary mismatch, forcing mismatch, and image-class scenarios are retained, including those in Appendix F.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments: FM, PBFM, Base AM, Base AM + φ, FM+ECI for elasticity, and vanilla Adjoint Matching for images. Tables 1–2 and 10–13 retain the same comparison rows.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the 256-sample evaluations, target-physics reference datasets, residual normalization, MMD/SSIM metrics, and training and sampling settings. Appendices B–E show no substantive protocol revisions.

E4.justification: The regularization/diversity sweeps, joint-flow ablations, elasticity residual heatmaps, and Stokes forcing-misspecification study are unchanged. The sparse-guidance and other sample analyses in Appendix F are also retained.

E5.justification: Shared-seed and fixed-seed disclosures, tabulated ± reporting, and plotted error bars are unchanged. No additional repeated-run information, uncertainty-estimation procedure, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results, and qualitative samples match. For example, Table 1 retains the proposed method's boundary error of 1.71×10^-6, and Table 2 retains its selected weak residual of 4.3. Appendix F results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The control formulation, weak-form derivations, and Lemma 1 with its proof remain unchanged. Section 3 restores omitted dt factors, and Appendix D.4 replaces 'limited' with 'bounded'; these are notation and wording corrections without revised mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about post-training physical consistency, joint solution–parameter generation without paired training data, diversity preservation, and applicability to natural images.

C2.justification: Interpretations of regularization versus diversity, joint-flow benefits, and severe forcing mismatch are unchanged. Appendix E.2 retains the qualification that the chosen misspecification settings disadvantage training-time PBFM.

D1.justification: v2 promises code and training-script release upon acceptance. v3 removes that promise and adds an explicit implementation repository link after the introduction. Hyperparameters, hardware, software, and implementation descriptions otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning relative to physics-informed learning, constrained diffusion, PBFM, ECI, and Adjoint Matching are unchanged. No cited work is added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 makes spelling and grammar corrections, merges some paragraphs, and corrects differential notation. It also adds author contacts and publication text and expands acknowledgments. The section sequence and scientific narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from PDF page 4 to page 3. Conference headers and text reflow change spacing and placement around existing displays. The same figures and tables are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 supplies a concrete implementation location where v2 promised a future release, improving access documentation. Wording and differential-notation corrections modestly improve clarity. The scientific evidence remains unchanged, and repository completeness cannot be established from the PDFs.
